record.original_question: Given an abstract polytope P, determine the size of its monodromy group |Mon(P)|.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Given a polytope P, determine | Mon(P)|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be an abstract polytope of rank n, that is, a partially ordered set with a minimum face F_{-1} and a maximum face F_n satisfying the standard axioms: every maximal chain (flag) has the same length n+2; P is strongly flag-connected; and for any two faces F < G with rank(G) - rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G (the diamond condition). Two flags of P are called i-adjacent if they differ exactly in their face of rank i. For each i in {0, 1, ..., n-1}, define a permutation σ_i of the set F(P) of flags of P by sending each flag Φ to its unique i-adjacent flag. The monodromy group of P is the subgroup
  Mon(P) := ⟨ σ_0, σ_1, ..., σ_{n-1} ⟩
of the symmetric group on F(P). Determine, as a function of the combinatorial data of P, the order |Mon(P)| of the monodromy group of P.
artifact.status_search_result: No general formula or algorithm for |Mon(P)| in terms of the combinatorial data of an arbitrary abstract polytope P is known. The literature has computed Mon(P) only for special families (e.g., regular polytopes, where Mon(P) is the automorphism group, and certain truncated simplices and other constructions), indicating that the general determination remains open.

status_evidence.title: Regular Covers and Monodromy Groups of Abstract Polytopes (Monson)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses monodromy groups Mon(P) of abstract polytopes and their relation to regular covers; computing Mon(P) is treated case by case.
status_evidence.claim: General determination of |Mon(P)| is approached only for special families, suggesting the general problem is open.

status_evidence.title: The monodromy group of a truncated simplex
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the monodromy group of truncated simplices in all ranks.
status_evidence.claim: Monodromy groups have been computed only for specific polytope families, not for general P.
